newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Stg recovers, eyes break of 2.9650 marks.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Stg recovers, eyes break of 2.9650 marks.

text.p: Sterling is poised to break first resistance at 2.9650 marks as it recovers from Thursday's slide to a low of 2.9506, chartists said.
The slightly firmer dollar tone is also lending a helping hand to the pound, while solid support in the 2.95 zone is likely to limit the downside again.

"Sterling/mark will recover, with 2.9650 being good resistance," said Stuart Frost, market analyst at NatWest Markets. "It is very well supported in the 2.95 zone, and I would only be worried below that level," he said.
At 0715 GMT sterling/mark was at 2.9630/40 marks.
That compared with 2.9566/76 in late European trading on Thursday. Sterling/dollar was at $1.6880/90 from $1.6882/92.

Another hurdle is the recent six-year high at 2.9760 marks ahead of strong resistance at 2.9825/50, a congestion zone dating back to 1991, analysts said. Above that band, there is little in the way to the psychologically important 3.0000 mark level.

A decline below 2.95 would increase the risk of a larger correction. "On a break of 2.95, sterling/mark would go back to the 2.9300/9200 support zone," said Gerry Celaya, senior technical analyst at American Express Bank.

Cable remained solid during Thursday's sterling/mark rollercoaster ride. A break above $1.6920 resistance would put major resistance at $1.70 into focus, once the recent high at $1.6959 is eroded, analysts said.
"A push through $1.6920 will open up $1.70," said Frost, adding that cable had good support in the $1.6800/40 area. -- Astrid Zweynert London newsroom + 44 171 542 7792
